div.head: Af 2.1
div.ab: Gif hine mon on ðam fierste geyflige mid slege oððe mid bende oððe þurh wunde, bete þara æghwelc mid ryhte ðeodscipe, ge mid were ge mid wite, ⁊ þam hiwum hundtwelftig scill. ciricfriðes to bote ⁊ næbbe his agne forfongen.

Gif hine man on þam fyrste geyflie mid slæge oððe mid bende oððe þurh wunde, bete ðæra æghwylc mid rihte þeowscipe, ge mid were ge mid wite, ⁊ þam hiwum CXX scll.' cyricfriðes bote ⁊ hæbbe his agen forfangen.
Si quis infra hunc terminum malignauerit eum in ictibus aut uinculis aut uerberibus, emendet singulum eorum rectitudine patrie wera et wita, et ecclesie ministris CXX solidos pro infractione pacis.

Gif hine mon on ðam fierste geyflige mid slege oððe mid bende oððe þurh wunde, bete þara æghwelc mid ryhte ðeodscipe, ge mid were ge mid wite, ⁊ þam hiwum hundtwelftig scill. ciricfriðes to bote ⁊ næbbe his agne forfongen.

Gif hine mon on ðam fierst geyflige mid slege oððe mid bende oððe þurh wunde, bete þara ægwhelc mid ryhte ðeodscipe, ge mid were ge mid wite, ⁊ þam hiwum hundtwelftig scill ciricfriðes to bote ⁊ næbbe his agne forfongen.

Wenn man ihn innerhalb dieser Frist schädigt mit Todtschlag oder mit Fesselung oder durch Wunden, so büsse man jedes davon nach gesetzlichem Rechtsbrauch, sowohl mit Wergeld als mit Strafgeld, und dem Convent 120 Schill. als Kirchenfriedensbusse. Und man habe [dadurch] die eigene [Busssumme, die der Flüchtling dem Verfolger schuldet] nicht erlangt.

If someone harms him within this term by slaying or by binding or through wounds, let him compensate for each of these according to lawful custom, both with wergeld and with fine, and [pay] the community 120 shillings as compensation for [breach of] church peace. And let him not [thereby] have obtained his own [compensation which the fugitive owes the pursuer].

If, during that time, anyone injures him by a [mortal] blow, [by putting him in] fetters, or by wounding him, he shall pay compensation for each of these offences in the regular way, both with wergeld and fine, and he shall pay 120 shillings to the community as compensation for violation of the sanctuary of the Church, and he [himself] shall not have the payment due to him from the fugitive.

If during that respite he is molested with slaying or binding or wounding, each of those [who did it] is to make amends according to the legal custom, both with wergild and with fine, and to pay to the community 120 shillings as compensation for the breach of sanctuary, and is to have forfeited his own [claim against the culprit].

If he is harmed during that time period with a blow or by binding or through a wound, let each of them compensate according to lawful regulations both with wergild and with fine, and to the household [of the minster] 120 shillings as compensation for [breach of] church peace, and he [who harmed him] shall not receive his own [compensation otherwise due him].

note.label: shared vocabulary
note.quote: This compound appears elsewhere only in the laws of Æthelberht (§6) [...] lends some support to Alfred's claim that he drew on Æthelberht's laws

note.seg: hæbbe So; ⁊ n. h. a. f. fehlt Ld Quadr.
hæbbe So; ⁊ n. h. a. f. lacking in Ld Quadr.
in i. a. nur Lond; fehlt R T Hk Br
in i. a. only Lond; lacking in R T Hk Br
‘aber’ fügt So hinzu. — Vgl. Gl Asylbruch 3
‘Schlag’ Frühere nach Q, der deshalb ‘Wunden’ fortlässt; aber 2 Z. weiter spricht Af vom Wergeld für ihn. — Hier binden (s. d. Gl 1a) darf man den, obschon erwiesenen, Missetäter nicht

‘blow’ earlier editors, following Q, who therefore omits ‘wounds’; but 2 ll. further on Af speaks of the wergild for him. — Here one may not bind (see that word in Gl 1a) the misdoer, even though his guilt is proven

þurhwunde ‘verwunde’ Frühere, auch Turk. Weder das Adj. þurhwund noch wundian berechtigen zu solcher Ansetzung. — Im Falle blosser Fesselung oder Wunde erhält Verfolgter nicht volles Wergeld, nur einen Teil davon

þurhwunde ‘wound’ earlier editors, Turk too. Neither the adj. þurhwund nor wundian justifies setting up such a form. — In the case of mere binding or wounding the pursued man does not receive the full wergild, only part of it
Q übersetzt silbenhaft þeod ‘Volk’. Allein das Kompositum heisst ‘disciplina’. H’s Variante, sonst nicht belegt, müsste ‘Dienstbarkeit’ heissen, was nicht passt: vielleicht blosse Verschreibung

Q translates þeod syllable by syllable as ‘people’. But the compound means ‘disciplina’. H’s variant, not otherwise attested, would have to mean ‘servitude’, which does not fit: perhaps a mere slip of the pen
Vielleicht wieder um Weltgeistliche einzuschliessen (s. o. 2¹): ‘Kirchendienern’ Q
Perhaps again in order to include the secular clergy (see above 2¹): ‘church servants’ Q

So’s Lesart ist späterer Zahlname. — 120 Schill., für blutig (s. Gl 6) Fechten im Kloster schon seit Ine, kostet später Friedensbruch einer Mittelkirche; ebd.: Asylbruch 5; Kirchenfriede 3. 4a. Es ist das [Königs] Ungehorsam (s. d. Gl 4b. 7), dem der Bruch des Kirchenfriedens auch sonst gleich wertet

So’s reading is a later form of the numeral. — 120 shill., the penalty for fighting with bloodshed (see Gl 6) in a monastery as early as Ine, is later the cost of breach of the peace of a middle-rank church; ibid.: Asylbruch 5; Kirchenfriede 3. 4a. It is the [king’s] disobedience (see that word in Gl 4b. 7), with which breach of the peace of the church is elsewhere too rated equal
bote ergänzen Schmid, Wülfing Syntax 184; ‘sein eigen’, aus H, Price-Thorpe. Price meint, der Flüchtling leide vielleicht Vermögenseinziehung. Allein dieser Subjektwechsel fiele auf
bote is supplied by Schmid and Wülfing Syntax 184; ‘his own’, from H, Price-Thorpe. Price thinks the fugitive perhaps suffers confiscation of property. But this change of subject would be striking

= ‘gesichert, fest erreicht’. Schon das 11. Jh. verstand den letzten Satz nicht mehr. Denn die Vorlage von Ld und Q lässt ihn ganz und H So die Negation fort. Thorpe läßt forfongen unübersetzt. Wilkins versteht H: ‘bona eius apprehendantur’, als wäre eine Konstruktion ‘er bekomme [= ihm werde] fortgenommen’ möglich. — Die Schreiber H So nahmen wohl forfongen im Sinne von Af 42, 4: hæbbe his mæg forworht [= quicquid adversus eum (Verfolgten) habebat forisfaciat Hn 83, 3] ‘Rächer habe [durch vorzeitige Rache den Anspruch aus des Verfolgten Totschlag gegen] seinen Verwandten verwirkt’. Solche Bed., in keinem German. Dialekt nachweisbar, aber angenommen von Price, Schmid, Toller, mochten sie folgern aus dem das Simplex bisweilen verneinenden Präfix for- (dt. ver-) in Analogie mit forbeodan, forgitan. Zu dieser Bed. ‘verloren’ mussten sie die Negation tilgen, um den authentischen Sinn dennoch richtig auszudrücken. Af meint: ‘berechtigter Verfolger verliere den Anspruch’, wie auch sonst, wegen Asylbruchs; s. d. Gl 5

= ‘secured, firmly obtained’. As early as the 11th cent. the last sentence was no longer understood. For the exemplar of Ld and Q omits it altogether, and H So omit the negation. Thorpe leaves forfongen untranslated. Wilkins understands H: ‘bona eius apprehendantur’, as if a construction ‘let him get [= let there be from him] taken away’ were possible. — The scribes of H So probably took forfongen in the sense of Af 42, 4: hæbbe his mæg forworht [= quicquid adversus eum (the pursued man) habebat forisfaciat Hn 83, 3] ‘let the avenger have forfeited [through premature vengeance the claim arising from the slaying of the pursued man against] his kinsman’. Such a meaning, demonstrable in no Germanic dialect but assumed by Price, Schmid and Toller, they may have inferred from the prefix for- (German ver-), which sometimes negates the simplex, by analogy with forbeodan, forgitan. To arrive at this meaning ‘lost’ they had to delete the negation in order still to express the authentic sense correctly. Af means: ‘a justified pursuer loses his claim’, as elsewhere too, on account of breach of sanctuary; see that word in Gl 5

note.label: forfongen
note.seg: næbbe h. a. f. omitted in Quad. & Ld.

Liebermann understands this to mean, ‘he (the pursuer) shall not have obtained the sum due to him’: i.e. by violating the right of asylum, he will lose what the fugitive owes him. But forfon does not seem to have this meaning elsewhere, while the syntax too is peculiar. Is it possible that in the archetype MS the reading was his agenne forfong, and that owing to an error of omission and a subsequent marginal correction, the en of ag[en]ne has been transposed to the end of the sentence? It is not stated that the pursuer has been robbed by the fugitive.
